_instructions: Third-party platforms EPAY can set a merchant up on when EPAY POS is not the right fit. Pages generate at /third-party/<slug>.
_note_on_claims: VERIFY BEFORE PUBLISHING. These descriptions are written from general knowledge of each platform, not from EPAY's own agreements. Three things to check: (1) that EPAY is actually authorised to resell or board merchants on each one, (2) that the wording does not imply a partnership or endorsement that does not exist, (3) trademark usage — do not add another company's logo without permission. Every platform name here is someone else's trademark.
_note_on_prices: NO PRICES. Hardware prices for other companies' devices vary by reseller, change often, and publishing them as if they were EPAY's price is a liability. Every item says 'Ask us' and routes to contact. If you want real prices here, supply the ones you actually sell at.
heading: When EPAY POS Isn't the Right Fit
lede: Some businesses are already committed to a platform, or need something EPAY POS doesn't do. We can board and support you on these instead — same team, same statement review, same local support.

platforms.name: Clover
platforms.summary: A widely used cloud POS with a large app marketplace and a full hardware range.
platforms.body: Clover is a cloud-based POS platform from Fiserv, used across restaurants, retail and services. Its strength is breadth — a large third-party app marketplace and a hardware line that spans a countertop station down to a handheld. Merchants already on Clover often want to keep the platform and change who supports and prices the processing behind it.
good_for: Merchants already on Clover who want better processing rates
Businesses that rely on a specific Clover app
Multi-site operators standardised on one platform

platforms.name: NRS
platforms.summary: National Retail Solutions — POS built specifically for independent convenience stores and bodegas.
platforms.body: NRS is aimed squarely at independent convenience stores, bodegas and small groceries. It ships with a large pre-built product catalogue for that trade, handles age-restricted items, and includes a customer-facing screen. It is a narrower product than a general POS, which is exactly why it fits the stores it is built for.
good_for: Independent convenience stores and bodegas
Stores that want a pre-loaded product catalogue
Operators running a cash discount programme

platforms.name: NCR
platforms.summary: One hardware family that runs several different POS software lines — restaurant, specialty retail, grocery and convenience.
platforms.body: NCR (now NCR Voyix) is one of the oldest names in point of sale, and its strength is range rather than a single product. The same terminals, handhelds and kitchen screens run whichever NCR software line fits the business — Aloha in a restaurant, Counterpoint in a specialty store, a scanning and self-checkout setup in a grocery. That matters for operators running more than one kind of location, or for anyone who has already standardised on NCR hardware and does not want to replace it to change what runs on top.
good_for: Grocery and supermarket operators running scanning lanes or self-checkout
Multi-unit and franchise restaurant groups on Aloha
Specialty retailers running NCR Counterpoint
Operators with mixed formats — a restaurant and a store under one owner
Anyone standardised on NCR hardware who wants to change what runs on it
platforms.software_note: Which of these we can board and support depends on the configuration. Tell us the format and we will tell you straight which line fits — including when EPAY POS is the better answer.

software.name: Aloha
software.body: NCR's restaurant platform, common in table service and multi-unit groups. Deep back office, franchise-level reporting and a long list of established integrations.

software.name: Counterpoint
software.body: Retail POS built around inventory — matrix items, purchasing and stock control across more than one store.

software.name: Grocery and supermarket
software.body: Scanning lanes, scale integration and self-checkout for stores moving serious volume through the front end.

software.name: Convenience and fuel
software.body: Forecourt control and age-restricted sales handled at the register, with the fuel position tied into the same system.

software.name: Third-party integrations
software.body: Accounting, payroll, loyalty and online ordering hang off the platform rather than being rebuilt inside it.

platforms.name: TSYS
platforms.summary: A major merchant acquirer and processor, now part of Global Payments.
platforms.body: TSYS is a processing platform rather than a POS. It sits behind the terminal, handling authorisation, settlement and funding. Merchants come to it for the processing relationship and the terminal estate that runs on it, rather than for front-of-house software.
good_for: Merchants who need a specific processing platform
Businesses keeping existing terminals
Anyone comparing acquirers on price
platforms.meta_description: TSYS is a major merchant acquirer and processor, now part of Global Payments. What it means for your card processing, from EPAY POS in Troy, MI.

platforms.name: Lodging with EPAY
platforms.summary: Payments for hotel property management systems, integrated through FreedomPay's FuseBox gateway.
platforms.body: Hotels have requirements a restaurant POS does not: payments have to integrate with the property management system, handle pre-authorisations at check-in and incrementals through the stay, and settle folios at check-out. We support that through FreedomPay's FuseBox gateway, which is the integration route most major hotel brands and PMS vendors certify against.
good_for: Branded properties whose PMS certifies against FreedomPay
Independent hotels needing PMS-integrated payments
Properties with food and beverage on the same folio

capabilities.name: PMS-Integrated Payments
capabilities.body: Card capture and settlement flow through the property management system, not a terminal sitting beside it.

capabilities.name: Pre-Auth and Incrementals
capabilities.body: Authorise at check-in and increment through the stay, so the folio settles cleanly at check-out.

capabilities.name: FuseBox Gateway
capabilities.body: FreedomPay's FuseBox is the integration layer most major PMS platforms certify against.

capabilities.name: Food and Beverage on Folio
capabilities.body: Restaurant and bar charges posted to the room, settled with the stay.

capabilities.name: Tokenisation
capabilities.body: Card data is tokenised at the gateway, so it never sits in the property's systems.

capabilities.name: Multi-Property Reporting
capabilities.body: Consolidated reporting across a portfolio rather than per-property exports.

platforms.name: Additional Gateways
platforms.summary: Gateway options for e-commerce, virtual terminals and custom integrations.
platforms.body: Where a business already has a website, a booking system or bespoke software, the payment side is a gateway rather than a POS. We can set you up on the common gateways so card payments run through your existing system instead of a new one.
good_for: E-commerce running on an existing platform
Booking and scheduling software that takes payment
Custom software needing an API

_note_on_vendor_images: Product photography on the Clover, NCR and NRS pages is the manufacturers' own, taken from their public product pages, and carries their logos on the devices. Clover's published media guidelines permit editorial use only and prohibit use 'in connection with advertisement, promotion, or sale' without separate written approval from Fiserv; the owner has directed that these go up on the strength of EPAY's reseller relationship. Get that in writing from Clover/Fiserv, NCR and NRS before launch, and swap in partner-portal assets if they supply them.
_note_on_terminals: Terminal and PIN pad photography is Ingenico's own, from their product pages at ingenico.com, because Ingenico is what EPAY mainly deploys. If EPAY ships a different model on any of these, swap the image and the spec line together — the spec names the model in the photo and the two must not drift apart.
